beats.text: Low pay, little tax, maybe none at all. The CRA can still pay you up to sixteen hundred and thirty-three dollars. Here's who gets it.
It's the Canada Workers Benefit. A refundable credit: it comes back to you even if you owe nothing.
For twenty twenty-five: up to sixteen hundred and thirty-three dollars single, twenty-eight hundred and thirteen for a family. You need working income over three thousand dollars.
Then it fades. Single, above twenty-six thousand eight hundred and fifty-five dollars, fifteen percent of the extra comes off.
Leo earned thirty thousand. That's three thousand one hundred and forty-five over, so four hundred and seventy-two less. Still about eleven hundred and sixty-one dollars.
The twist: you don't have to wait for the refund. Up to half can be paid to you in advance, during the year.
So claim it when you file: Schedule six, line forty-five three hundred.
Next: your friend got benefits and you got nothing. Here's why. Follow so you don't miss it.
